claim: RNA-Seq was performed on the whole olfactory mucosa of male and female mice at various ages housed under sex-separated conditions after weaning.
source: We first performed RNA-Seq on the whole olfactory mucosa of male and female mice at various ages housed under sex-separated conditions after weaning (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the experimental procedure performed.

claim: Differential expression analysis of ORs revealed no obvious sexually dimorphic OR expression at 3 weeks (weaning) age.
source: Differential expression analysis of ORs revealed no obvious sexually dimorphic OR expression at 3 weeks (weaning) age.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from differential expression analysis.

claim: Progressive differential expression analysis of ORs at 9, 26, and 43 weeks age revealed at least three OR genes, Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295, to exhibit growing and robust enrichment in female mice.
source: In contrast, progressive differential expression analysis of ORs at 9, 26, and 43 weeks age revealed at least three OR genes, Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295, to exhibit growing and robust enrichment in female mice (male enriched ORs are discussed later; Figure 1B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from differential expression analysis and referenced figures.

claim: At 43 weeks old, Olfr910 exhibited log2FC = 2.19 with FDR < 6.71E-26.
source: at 43 weeks old: Olfr910 log2FC = 2.19 FDR < 6.71E-26
evidence: This is a specific statistical result from the differential expression analysis.

claim: At 43 weeks old, Olfr912 exhibited log2FC = 1.97 with FDR < 3.41E-14.
source: Olfr912 log2FC = 1.97 FDR < 3.41E-14
evidence: This is a specific statistical result from the differential expression analysis.

claim: At 43 weeks old, Olfr1295 exhibited log2FC = 2.55 with FDR < 5.83E-19.
source: Olfr1295 log2FC = 2.55 FDR < 5.83E-19
evidence: This is a specific statistical result from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Past work demonstrated a correlation between OR transcript abundance and the number of OSNs expressing those ORs.
source: Past work demonstrating a correlation between OR transcript abundance and the number of OSNs expressing those ORs led us to quantify the number of OSNs expressing these ORs (Khan et al., 2011; Ibarra-Soria et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The proportion of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 was greater in 43-week-old female mice than in 43-week-old male mice (all p < 0.0001, unpaired two-tailed t-test).
source: The results of the in situ mRNA hybridization demonstrated that the proportion of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 was greater in 43-week-old female mice than in 43-week-old male mice (all p < 0.0001, unpaired two-tailed t-test; Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ mRNA hybridization data and statistical analysis.

claim: The subpopulation of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 are over-represented in sex-separated female mice compared to sex-separated male mice.
source: Altogether, these results demonstrate that the subpopulation of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 are over-represented in sex-separated female mice compared to sex-separated male mice.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the RNA-Seq and in situ hybridization data.

claim: Juvenile mice were exposed to either a blank odor cassette (control), mature male mice, mature female mice, or 10 μL of 1% (v/v) acetophenone spotted onto blotting paper placed inside an odor cassette.
source: To test this hypothesis, we briefly exposed juvenile mice (~3 weeks old) to either a blank odor cassette (control), mature male mice, mature female mice, or 10 μL of 1% (v/v) acetophenone spotted onto blotting paper placed inside an odor cassette (Figure 3A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design for testing OSN activation.

claim: The population of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 displayed elevated pS6 staining intensity only when exposed to mature male mice (all p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction).
source: Double in situ mRNA hybridization and immunostaining revealed the population of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 to display elevated pS6 staining intensity only when exposed to mature male mice (all p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction; Figure 3B–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data and statistical analysis.

claim: Exposure to mature female mice or acetophenone did not lead to significant pS6 induction in the population of OSNs expressing either Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 (all p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction).
source: Exposure to mature female mice or acetophenone did not lead to significant pS6 induction in the population of OSNs expressing either Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 (all p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction; Figure 3B–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data and statistical analysis.

claim: The subpopulation of OSNs that express Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 are responders to the natural scent of mature male mice.
source: Altogether, these results demonstrate that the subpopulation of OSNs that express Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 to be responders to the natural scent of mature male mice.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the pS6 immunostaining data.

claim: Exposure to 10 μL of 0.01% (v/v) SBT led to the lowest false discovery rate (FDR) and greatest enrichment of transcripts for Olfr910 and Olfr912 from activated OSNs (at an FDR < 0.05), compared to all other ORs.
source: Indeed, exposure to 10 μL of 0.01% (v/v) SBT led to the lowest false discovery rate (FDR) and greatest enrichment of transcripts for Olfr910 and Olfr912 from activated OSNs (at an FDR < 0.05), compared to all other ORs, suggesting OSNs expressing Olfr910 and Olfr912 to be the most robustly responding OSNs for SBT in vivo (Olfr910 log2FC = 2.88 FDR < 1.47E-25, Olfr912 log2FC = 3.10 FDR < 2.78E-36; Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by pS6-IP-Seq data and statistical analysis.

claim: OSNs expressing Olfr910 and Olfr912 are the most robustly responding OSNs for SBT in vivo.
source: suggesting OSNs expressing Olfr910 and Olfr912 to be the most robustly responding OSNs for SBT in vivo (Olfr910 log2FC = 2.88 FDR < 1.47E-25, Olfr912 log2FC = 3.10 FDR < 2.78E-36; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the pS6-IP-Seq data showing the lowest FDR and greatest enrichment.

claim: Exposure to 10 μL of 100 μM MTMT led to the lowest FDR and greatest enrichment of transcripts for Olfr1295 from activated OSNs (at an FDR < 0.05), compared to all other ORs.
source: Similarly, exposure to 10 μL of 100 μM MTMT led to the lowest FDR and greatest enrichment of transcripts for Olfr1295 from activated OSNs (at an FDR < 0.05), compared to all other ORs, suggesting OSNs expressing Olfr1295 to be the most robustly responding OSNs for MTMT in vivo (Olfr1295 log2FC = 1.80 FDR < 3.72E-5; Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by pS6-IP-Seq data and statistical analysis.

claim: OSNs expressing Olfr1295 are the most robustly responding OSNs for MTMT in vivo.
source: suggesting OSNs expressing Olfr1295 to be the most robustly responding OSNs for MTMT in vivo (Olfr1295 log2FC = 1.80 FDR < 3.72E-5; Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the pS6-IP-Seq data showing the lowest FDR and greatest enrichment.

claim: OSNs expressing Olfr910 and Olfr912 displayed increasingly intense pS6 immunostaining following exposure to SBT in a concentration-dependent manner (Olfr910: 0.01% SBT p < 0.0001, 0.1% SBT p < 0.0001, 1% SBT p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction, Olfr912: 0.01% SBT p < 0.01, 0.1% SBT p < 0.0001, 1% SBT p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction).
source: In situ mRNA hybridization probing for the expression of Olfr910 and Olfr912 followed by immunostaining for pS6 showed OSNs expressing Olfr910 and Olfr912 to display increasingly intense pS6 immunostaining following exposure to SBT in a concentration-dependent manner (Olfr910: 0.01% SBT p < 0.0001, 0.1% SBT p < 0.0001, 1% SBT p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction, Olfr912: 0.01% SBT p < 0.01, 0.1% SBT p < 0.0001, 1% SBT p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction; Figure 4E–F, Figure 4—figure supplement 3A-B).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and immunostaining data with statistical analysis.

claim: OSNs expressing Olfr1295 displayed increasingly intense pS6 immunostaining following exposure to MTMT in a concentration-dependent manner (100 μM MTMT p < 0.0001, 10 mM MTMT p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction).
source: Similarly, OSNs expressing Olfr1295, identified by in situ mRNA hybridization, displayed increasingly intense pS6 immunostaining following exposure to MTMT, again, in a concentration-dependent manner (100 μM MTMT p < 0.0001, 10 mM MTMT p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction; Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and immunostaining data with statistical analysis.

claim: OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 did not display significant pS6 signal intensity differences following exposure to acetophenone compared to control conditions (p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction).
source: OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 also did not display significant pS6 signal intensity differences following exposure to acetophenone compared to control conditions (p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons test correction; Figure 4E–G)
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and immunostaining data with statistical analysis.

claim: There was no sex bias in OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 by pS6 signal intensity induction after exposure to either SBT or MTMT (p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test correction).
source: We did not observe any sex bias in OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 by pS6 signal intensity induction after exposure to either SBT or MTMT, indicating a lack of sexual dimorphism in the response of OSNs to these stimuli (p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test correction; Figure 5A–C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data and statistical analysis.

claim: Differential expression analysis of ORs from the whole olfactory mucosa from sex-combined male and female mice revealed a severe attenuation of the dimorphic expression of Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 (at 43 weeks old: Olfr910 log2FC = 0.80 FDR > 0.65, Olfr912 log2FC = 0.59 FDR > 0.76, Olfr1295 log2FC = 0.76 FDR > 0.70).
source: Differential expression analysis of ORs from the whole olfactory mucosa from sex-combined male and female mice revealed a severe attenuation of the dimorphic expression of Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 (at 43 weeks old: Olfr910 log2FC = 0.80 FDR > 0.65, Olfr912 log2FC = 0.59 FDR > 0.76, Olfr1295 log2FC = 0.76 FDR > 0.70; Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by differential expression analysis data.

claim: Sex-separated female mice had an over-representation of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 (all p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test correction).
source: Sex-separated female mice had an over-representation of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 (all p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test correction; Figure 6D–F)
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data and statistical analysis.

claim: Mice from sex-combined conditions (sex-combined female, sex-combined male, and sex-separated male) were all comparable in OSN density expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 (p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test correction).
source: while mice from other conditions were all comparable (p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test correction; Figure 6D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data and statistical analysis.

claim: Cohabitation with the opposite sex, potentially via olfactory experience, is sufficient to attenuate the over-representation of the subpopulation of sexually dimorphic OSNs in sex-separated female mice.
source: These findings demonstrate cohabitation with the opposite sex, potentially via olfactory experience, is sufficient to attenuate the over-representation of the subpopulation of sexually dimorphic OSNs in sex-separated female mice.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the sex-combined housing data.

claim: RNA-Seq data identified over-expression of Olfr1437 and Olfr235 in sex-separated male mice.
source: In addition to identifying populations of OSNs over-represented in female mice, our RNA-Seq data also identified over-expression of Olfr1437 and Olfr235 in sex-separated male mice.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the RNA-Seq results.

claim: Olfr1437 and Olfr235 failed to exhibit robust sexually dimorphic expression when mice were housed in a sex-combined fashion.
source: Like female mouse over-represented ORs, Olfr1437 and Olfr235 failed to exhibit robust sexually dimorphic expression when mice were housed in a sex-combined fashion (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data comparing sex-separated and sex-combined housing.

claim: The proportion of OSNs expressing Olfr1437 was greater in 43-week-old male mice than in 43-week-old female mice (p < 0.0001, unpaired two-tailed t-test).
source: The results of in situ mRNA hybridization demonstrated that the proportion of OSNs expressing Olfr1437 to be greater in 43-week-old male mice than in 43-week-old female mice (p < 0.0001, unpaired two-tailed t-test; Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data and statistical analysis.

claim: The macrocyclic musk odorant cyclopentadecanone (CPD) was identified as an agonist for OSNs expressing Olfr1437 and Olfr235.
source: In our search for ligands activating sexually dimorphic ORs, we identified the macrocyclic musk odorant cyclopentadecanone (CPD; Figure 7D) as an agonist for OSNs expressing Olfr1437 and Olfr235 (Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is supported by pS6-IP-Seq data identifying CPD as an agonist.

claim: Musk or musk-related odorants activate sexually dimorphic, male-enriched populations of OSNs.
source: These results suggest musk or musk-related odorants to activate sexually dimorphic, male-enriched populations of OSNs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the CPD and muscone data.

claim: UMAP representations of mature OSN gene expressions, independent of chemosensory receptors, revealed sensory cells expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 to segregate toward a single extreme region while remaining far and distinct from sensory cells expressing Olfr1437 or Olfr235.
source: UMAP representations of mature OSN gene expressions, independent of chemosensory receptors, revealed sensory cells expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 to segregate toward a single extreme region while remaining far and distinct from sensory cells expressing Olfr1437 or Olfr235 (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-Seq data analysis and UMAP visualization.

claim: Expression analysis revealed an enrichment of S100a5, Ptprn, Pcp4l1, and Nrp1 amongst OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295.
source: Expression analysis revealed an enrichment of S100a5, Ptprn, Pcp4l1, and Nrp1 amongst OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295.
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: Enrichment of S100a5, Ptprn, Pcp4l1, and Nrp1 had been shown to occur in the literature as a function of neural activity.
source: Importantly, enrichment of these genes had been shown to occur in the literature as a function of neural activity (Figure 8B–C; Imai et al., 2006; Nakashima et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Odor experience significantly influences gene expression in OSNs, via an activity-dependent process relying on ligand-receptor interactions, to drive dimorphic representations of Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295.
source: Since the singly sequenced mature OSNs from Brann et al., 2020 were collected from mature male mice, who self-expose to MTMT and SBT, these results are consistent with the idea that odor experience significantly influences gene expression in OSNs, via an activity-dependent process relying on ligand-receptor interactions, to drive dimorphic representations of Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295.
evidence: This is an inference based on the single-cell RNA-Seq data and the known exposure of male mice to MTMT and SBT.

claim: Differential expression analysis of RNA sequenced whole olfactory mucosa tissues from sex-separated 26-week-old Bax-/- male and female mice revealed an overall lack of sexual dimorphism in the expression of Olfr910, Olfr912, Olfr1295, Olfr1437, and Olfr235.
source: Compared to wild-type mice, differential expression analysis of RNA sequenced whole olfactory mucosa tissues from sex-separated 26-week-old Bax-/- male and female mice revealed an overall lack of sexual dimorphism in the expression of Olfr910, Olfr912, Olfr1295, Olfr1437, and Olfr235 (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by differential expression analysis data from Bax-/- mice.

claim: In situ mRNA hybridization probing for the proportional abundance of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 demonstrated no significant differences between sex-separated Bax-/- male and female mice by 43 weeks age (p > 0.05, unpaired two-tailed t-test).
source: Additionally, in situ mRNA hybridization probing for the proportional abundance of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295, demonstrated no significant differences between sex-separated Bax-/- male and female mice by 43 weeks age (p > 0.05, unpaired two-tailed t-test; Figure 9B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data and statistical analysis from Bax-/- mice.

claim: The mechanisms underlying the generation of sexual dimorphism in the MOE are Bax-dependent and therefore likely driven by activity-dependent modulations in OSN lifespan.
source: While differential expression analysis comparing Bax-/- mice to wild-type mice revealed the expression of many ORs to change (Figure 9—figure supplement 2A-B), our results are consistent with the idea that the mechanisms underlying the generation of sexual dimorphism in the MOE are Bax-dependent and therefore likely driven by activity-dependent modulations in OSN lifespan.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Bax-/- data showing lack of sexual dimorphism.

claim: Olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) found in the MOE express a single olfactory receptor (OR) in a monoallelic fashion out of a large and diverse family of over 1000 candidate genes.
source: Olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) found in the MOE express a single olfactory receptor (OR) in a monoallelic fashion out of a large and diverse family of over 1000 candidate genes (Buck and Axel, 1991; Zhang and Firestein, 2002)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational literature.

claim: Odor recognition at the level of OSNs follows a combinatorial coding scheme where one OR can be activated by a set of odorants and one odorant can activate a combination of ORs.
source: Odor recognition at the level of OSNs additionally has been shown to follow a combinatorial coding scheme where one OR can be activated by a set of odorants and one odorant can activate a combination of ORs (Malnic et al., 1999; Jiang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Through combinatorial coding, it has been postulated that organisms, including mice and humans, can detect and discriminate against a myriad of odor molecules.
source: Through such combinatorial coding, it has been postulated that organisms, including mice and humans, can detect and discriminate against a myriad of odor molecules.
evidence: This is a statement of a postulate based on the combinatorial coding principle.

claim: SBT is a male-specific semiochemical.
source: the male-specific semiochemical SBT
evidence: This is stated as a known property of SBT.

claim: MTMT is a male-specific semiochemical.
source: the male-specific semiochemical MTMT
evidence: This is stated as a known property of MTMT.

claim: All of the identified sexually dimorphic populations of OSNs (Olfr910, Olfr912, Olfr1295, Olfr1437, and Olfr235) were localized to the ventral region of the MOE.
source: It is interesting to note, all of the identified sexually dimorphic populations of OSNs (Olfr910, Olfr912, Olfr1295, Olfr1437, and Olfr235) were localized to the ventral region of the MOE (Tan and Xie, 2018; Hu et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature on OR localization.

claim: Past work showed a robust response in the ventral region of the olfactory bulb to male mouse urine.
source: These results are consistent with past work showing a robust response in the ventral region of the olfactory bulb to male mouse urine (Lin et al., 2005; Xu et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Past findings showed a direct projection from a subset of ventrally localized olfactory bulb mitral cells to the amygdala.
source: Based on past findings showing a direct projection from a subset of ventrally localized olfactory bulb mitral cells to the amygdala (Kang et al., 2009; Inokuchi et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A subset, or even all, of the sexually dimorphic populations of OSNs may innervate olfactory bulb mitral cells that project to the amygdala.
source: it is tempting to speculate that a subset, or even all, of these sexually dimorphic populations of OSNs innervate these previously identified olfactory bulb mitral cells that project to the amygdala.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the ventral localization and known projections.

claim: SBT has been previously implicated in inducing the Whitten effect.
source: Past implications of SBT also inducing the Whitten effect (Jemiolo et al., 1986)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: MTMT has been previously implicated in influencing female mouse attractive behaviors.
source: Past implications of MTMT influencing female mouse attractive behaviors (Lin et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The over-representation of Olfr910 and Olfr912 may serve to enhance SBT detection for mediation of the Whitten effect.
source: Past implications of SBT also inducing the Whitten effect (Jemiolo et al., 1986) along with our finding of Olfr910 and Olfr912 to be robustly responsive to SBT and over-represented in sex-separated female mice lead us to speculate that the over-representation of these ORs serves to enhance SBT detection for mediation of the Whitten effect.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the data and previous literature.

claim: The over-representation of Olfr1295 may serve to enhance MTMT detection for mediating attractive responses.
source: Past implications of MTMT influencing female mouse attractive behaviors (Lin et al., 2005) along with our finding of Olfr1295 to be robustly responsive to MTMT and over-represented in sex-separated female mice lead us to speculate over-representation of this OR to serve to enhance MTMT detection for mediating attractive responses.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the data and previous literature.

claim: The MOE has the capacity to regenerate throughout the life of an animal.
source: Given the capacity of the MOE to regenerate throughout the life of an animal (Fletcher et al., 2011; Brann and Firestein, 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activity-mediated mechanisms may individualize the olfactory system by influencing OSN population dynamics.
source: it has been suggested that activity-mediated mechanisms may "individualize" the olfactory system by influencing OSN population dynamics (Ibarra-Soria et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Changes in OSN population dynamics following cohabitation for OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 are in part mediated by olfactory experience with SBT and MTMT.
source: we propose that changes in OSN population dynamics following cohabitation for OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295, are in part mediated by olfactory experience with SBT and MTMT.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the data showing attenuation of dimorphism with cohabitation and the identification of SBT and MTMT as ligands.

claim: The lengthy timeframes necessary to generate the observed differences are consistent with the hypothesis of modulation of OSN lifespan by activity.
source: The lengthy timeframes necessary to generate the differences that we observe are consistent with the hypothesis of modulation of OSN lifespan by activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the longitudinal data showing progressive changes over weeks.

claim: The form of plasticity observed appears to employ a distinct time course from reports of learning and fear conditioning influencing glomerular responses or proportional abundance of OSNs expressing ORs responsive to the fear-conditioned odor.
source: Additionally, the form of plasticity we observe here appears to employ a distinct time course from reports of learning and fear conditioning influencing the glomerular responses (Kass et al., 2013; Abraham et al., 2014) or proportional abundance of OSNs expressing ORs responsive to the fear-conditioned odor (Jones et al., 2008; Dias and Ressler, 2014; Morrison et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison to previous literature on fear conditioning.

claim: In the case of fear conditioning to acetophenone, the number of OSNs expressing M71 (Olfr151) appears to profoundly upregulate within just 3 weeks.
source: In the case of fear conditioning to acetophenone, the number of OSNs expressing M71 (Olfr151) appears to profoundly upregulate within just 3 weeks.
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings in the literature.

claim: By 9 weeks (~6 weeks post-weaning), Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 are not significantly differentially expressed (Olfr910 log2FC = 0.54 FDR > 0.24, Olfr912 log2FC = −0.26 FDR > 0.64, Olfr1295 log2FC = 0.65 FDR > 0.12).
source: In contrast, even by 9 weeks (~6 weeks post-weaning), Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 are not significantly differentially expressed (Olfr910 log2FC = 0.54 FDR > 0.24, Olfr912 log2FC = −0.26 FDR > 0.64, Olfr1295 log2FC = 0.65 FDR > 0.12; Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by differential expression analysis data.

claim: There may exist a multitude of distinct mechanisms, operating at non-identical time scales, to influence OSN population dynamics.
source: Altogether, these observations lead us to speculate the existence of a multitude of distinct mechanisms, operating at non-identical time scales, to influence OSN population dynamics.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the comparison of different plasticity time courses.

claim: Macrocyclic musk odorants are sex-specific in nature, including in the Moschus (musk deer) and Ondatra (muskrat) species.
source: Given the sex-specificity of macrocyclic musk odorants in nature, including in the Moschus (musk deer) and Ondatra (muskrat) species, it has been theorized that this family of odorants may be involved in chemical communication, potentially encoding information about the sex and maturity of an individual (Li et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Macrocyclic musk odorants may be involved in chemical communication, potentially encoding information about the sex and maturity of an individual.
source: it has been theorized that this family of odorants may be involved in chemical communication, potentially encoding information about the sex and maturity of an individual (Li et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The finding of over-represented OSN subpopulations robustly responsive to male-specific semiochemicals decreasing in proportional abundance in sex-separated females following sex-combined housing is consistent with the literature.
source: The finding of over-represented OSN subpopulations robustly responsive to male-specific semiochemicals to decrease in proportional abundance in sex-separated females following sex-combined housing, while consistent with the literature (Xu et al., 2016; Ibarra-Soria et al., 2017; van der Linden et al., 2018), is unexpected.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Once females receive exposure to male-specific semiochemicals, their detectability for semiochemicals slowly decreases over time, reflecting a potential homeostatic gain control mechanism for salient cue detection at the level of primary sensory neurons.
source: The results suggest that once females receive exposure to male-specific semiochemicals, their detectability for semiochemicals slowly decreases over time, reflecting a potential homeostatic "gain control" mechanism for salient cue detection at the level of primary sensory neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data showing decreased OSN abundance after exposure.

claim: Loss of Bax causes changes in the expression of many ORs when compared with wild-type controls.
source: Although loss of Bax causes changes in the expression of many ORs when compared with wild-type controls (Figure 9—figure supplement 2A-B)
evidence: This claim is supported by differential expression analysis data.

claim: The lack of robust sexual dimorphism in sex-separated Bax-/- mice may be a result of the lack of Bax-regulated activity-dependent alteration of sensory neuron lifespan.
source: we speculate the lack of robust sexual dimorphism in sex-separated Bax-/- mice to be a result of the lack of Bax-regulated activity-dependent alteration of sensory neuron lifespan.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the Bax-/- data.

claim: Bax-/- mice show an expanded olfactory epithelial thickness.
source: Since Bax-/- mice also show an expanded olfactory epithelial thickness (Robinson et al., 2003)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The lack of robust sexually dimorphic representation of ORs in Bax-/- mice may be a consequence of the expansion of OSNs expressing other ORs responding to self-generated or environmental cues.
source: the lack of the robust sexually dimorphic representation of ORs may also be a consequence of the expansion of OSNs expressing other ORs responding to self-generated or environmental cues.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the expanded epithelium in Bax-/- mice.

claim: ORs are expressed in highly stereotyped locations.
source: Despite the early discoveries of ORs being expressed in highly stereotyped locations, the functional consequences of these zonal expression distributions have remained unclear (Ressler et al., 1993; Vassar et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational literature.

claim: The functional consequences of zonal expression distributions of ORs have remained unclear.
source: Despite the early discoveries of ORs being expressed in highly stereotyped locations, the functional consequences of these zonal expression distributions have remained unclear (Ressler et al., 1993; Vassar et al., 1993).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The expression of many activity-associated genes was previously shown to be changed as a function of OSN activity using surgical strategies like unilateral naris occlusion.
source: Importantly, the expression of many of these same genes was also previously shown to be changed as a function of OSN activity using surgical strategies like unilateral naris occlusion (Wang et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The expression of many activity-associated genes was previously shown to be changed as a function of OSN activity using transgenic strategies like knock-in expression of constitutively active Gs.
source: and transgenic strategies like knock-in expression of constitutively active Gs (Imai et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The expression of many activity-associated genes was previously shown to be changed as a function of OSN activity using transgenic strategies like knock-in expression of wild-type and activity-deficient mutant non-OR G-protein coupled receptors.
source: and knock-in expression of wild-type and activity-deficient mutant non-OR G-protein coupled receptors (Nakashima et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Activity-associated enriched genes were not enriched in singly sequenced mature OSNs expressing Olfr1437 and Olfr235.
source: Furthermore, these same activity-associated enriched genes were not enriched in singly sequenced mature OSNs expressing Olfr1437 and Olfr235, consistent with the idea that male mice do not generate agonists for these ORs (see summary statistics files; Figure 8A-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: Male mice do not generate agonists for Olfr1437 and Olfr235.
source: consistent with the idea that male mice do not generate agonists for these ORs
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of activity-associated gene enrichment in OSNs expressing these ORs.

claim: UMAP representations emphasize local distances while preserving global structure.
source: Since UMAP representations emphasize local distances while preserving global structure
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of UMAP as a dimensionality reduction technique.

claim: The mechanism by which OR activity influences OSN gene expression to potentially drive the generation of the sexually dimorphic representations of Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 is not specific to OSNs expressing these ORs.
source: these results lead us to speculate that the mechanism by which OR activity influences OSN gene expression to potentially drive the generation of the sexually dimorphic representations of Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 is not specific to OSNs expressing these ORs.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the UMAP analysis showing overlap with other OSNs.

claim: Mechanisms like the basal level of OR activity may be implicated in OR-dependent OSN representation.
source: The overlap between OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 with OSNs expressing other ORs in the UMAP embedding also indicates mechanisms like the basal level of OR activity may be implicated in OR-dependent OSN representation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the UMAP analysis showing overlap.

claim: There may exist a vectorizable axis of OR activity influencing OSN gene expression and representation.
source: Such a finding would be consistent with the idea of a vectorizable axis of OR activity influencing OSN gene expression and representation.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the data.

claim: If female mice naturally produce ligands for OSNs expressing Olfr1437 and Olfr235, and the mechanism of the dimorphic representation is driven by activity, then OSNs expressing Olfr1437 and Olfr235 would be expected to segregate to a single extreme region when harvested from mature female mice.
source: Similarly, if female mice naturally produce ligands for OSNs expressing Olfr1437 and Olfr235, and the mechanism of the dimorphic representation of Olfr1437 and Olfr235 is driven by activity like we speculate for Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295, then we would expect OSNs expressing Olfr1437 and Olfr235 to segregate to a single extreme region when harvested from mature female mice and compared to many other mature OSNs harvested from mature female mice.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conditional speculation.

claim: Plasticity within the OSN population can be postulated to enable adaptation of an individual's olfactory system for the sensitive detection of salient odors, which may vary from one environment to another.
source: Plasticity within the OSN population can be postulated to enable adaptation of an individual's olfactory system for the sensitive detection of salient odors, which may vary from one environment to another.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a postulate.

claim: Sex-specific chemical cues have been implicated in instinctual behaviors and physiological responses.
source: While sex-specific chemical cues have been implicated in instinctual behaviors and physiological responses (Novotny et al., 1985; Jemiolo et al., 1986; Sam et al., 2001; Chamero et al., 2007; Haga et al., 2010; Dewan et al., 2013; Ferrero et al., 2013; Li et al., 2013; Haga-Yamanaka et al., 2014; Fu et al., 2015; Hattori et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: The degree to which animals are exposed to sex-specific chemical cues in nature may vary substantially among individuals.
source: the degree to which animals are exposed to these chemical cues in nature may vary substantially among individuals.
evidence: This is a statement about natural variation in exposure.

claim: A report by van der Linden et al., 2018 also identified sexually dimorphic expression of a subset of ORs using a combination of sequencing and histology-based approaches.
source: A report by van der Linden et al., 2018 also identified sexually dimorphic expression of a subset of ORs using a combination of sequencing and histology-based approaches.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The data from this study agree with van der Linden et al., 2018 in the identification of the sexually dimorphic expression of Olfr910, Olfr912, Olfr1295, Olfr1437, and Olfr235 in mice housed in a sex-separated manner.
source: Our data agree in the following manner: identification of the sexually dimorphic expression of Olfr910, Olfr912, Olfr1295, Olfr1437, and Olfr235 in mice housed in a sex-separated manner
evidence: This is a statement of agreement with previous literature based on the data.

claim: The data from this study agree with van der Linden et al., 2018 in the demonstration of activation of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 following exposure to mature male mice.
source: demonstration of activation of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 following exposure to mature male mice
evidence: This is a statement of agreement with previous literature based on the data.

claim: The data from this study agree with van der Linden et al., 2018 in showing a general lack of sexual dimorphism in OR expression in mice housed in a sex-combined manner.
source: a general lack of sexual dimorphism in OR expression in mice housed in a sex-combined manner.
evidence: This is a statement of agreement with previous literature based on the data.

claim: The findings of experience to influence OSN population dynamics suggest a role of experience in adjusting an animal's sensitivity to salient chemical cue detection.
source: Together, our findings of experience to influence OSN population dynamics suggest a role of experience in adjusting an animal's sensitivity to salient chemical cue detection.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data showing experience-dependent changes.

claim: Other ORs activated by SBT and MTMT did not exhibit sexual dimorphism.
source: Remarkably, other ORs activated by SBT and MTMT did not exhibit sexual dimorphism.
evidence: This is a statement about the specificity of the sexual dimorphism to certain ORs.

claim: When other sex-specific and sex-enriched odorants were tested, OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 were not activated.
source: Furthermore, when we tested other sex-specific and sex-enriched odorants, we did not observe activation of OSNs expressing Olfr910, Olfr912, or Olfr1295 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by pS6-IP-Seq data.

claim: Cognate receptors for other sex-specific and sex-enriched odorants did not exhibit sexually dimorphic expression.
source: nor did cognate receptors for these other odors exhibit sexually dimorphic expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by differential expression analysis data.

claim: Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 have a specialized role in conveying a salient signal about SBT and MTMT from the olfactory periphery to the central nervous system.
source: These results altogether lead us to hypothesize a specialized role for Olfr910, Olfr912, and Olfr1295 in conveying a salient signal about SBT and MTMT from the olfactory periphery to the central nervous system.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a hypothesis based on the specificity of the responses and dimorphism.

claim: Behavioral and physiological responses to semiochemicals have traditionally been viewed as genetically predetermined and 'hardwired.'
source: That is, while behavioral and physiological responses to semiochemicals have traditionally been viewed as genetically predetermined and 'hardwired,' there may exist a significant context and experience-dependent flexibility.
evidence: This is a statement about the traditional view in the field.

claim: There may exist a significant context and experience-dependent flexibility in behavioral and physiological responses to semiochemicals.
source: there may exist a significant context and experience-dependent flexibility.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the findings of plasticity.

claim: Group housed sex-separated female mice exhibit a general suppression and irregularity in estrous cycling.
source: For example, it has been previously shown that group housed sex-separated female mice exhibit a general suppression and irregularity in estrous cycling.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to previous literature (though specific citations are not provided in this sentence).

claim: Upon exposure to a mature male mouse, unisexually grouped female mice often rapidly and synchronously enter into estrus (Whitten effect).
source: Upon exposure to a mature male mouse, these unisexually grouped female mice often rapidly and synchronously enter into estrus (Whitten effect) (Whitten, 1956; Whitten, 1957; Whitten, 1959; Whitten et al., 1968; Gangrade and Dominic, 1984).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: The over-representation of Olfr910 and Olfr912 in sex-separated female mice may serve to enhance SBT detection for mediation of the Whitten effect.
source: Past implications of SBT also inducing the Whitten effect (Jemiolo et al., 1986) along with our finding of Olfr910 and Olfr912 to be robustly responsive to SBT and over-represented in sex-separated female mice lead us to speculate that the over-representation of these ORs serves to enhance SBT detection for mediation of the Whitten effect.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the data and previous literature.

claim: The over-representation of Olfr1295 in sex-separated female mice may serve to enhance MTMT detection for mediating attractive responses.
source: Past implications of MTMT influencing female mouse attractive behaviors (Lin et al., 2005) along with our finding of Olfr1295 to be robustly responsive to MTMT and over-represented in sex-separated female mice lead us to speculate over-representation of this OR to serve to enhance MTMT detection for mediating attractive responses.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the data and previous literature.
